newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes flat with NYMEX, heavy supply.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes flat with NYMEX, heavy supply.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices held at yesterday's levels in light midday discussion, traders said, in reaction to steady West Texas Intermediate (WTI) values.
October WTI traded at $23.25/23.35 a barrel early, flat from Monday with U.S. refiners waiting for lower prices should Mideast tensions ease.
Outright prices for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude remained $20.85/21.15, the same as late Monday, with sellers looking for buyers. Traders said weak fundamentals kept buyers from making bids.
Planned and unplanned outages in PADD 5 West Coast have kept refining capacity in the range of 88 percent the last week, below the usual range of mid-90s.
And that left extra light and heavy crudes in the market, just before the start of refinery maintenance season.
Arco announced it will restart a coker at its Carson, Calif., refinery September 21 following a roughly two-week shutdown for repairs.
Deltas for Line 63 widened by about 50 cents to $3.20/3.00 a barrel under WTI following a purported deal late last week.
California heavy grades were seen flat, but some traders claimed deltas had risen above the current range of 50 to 25 cents under posted prices.
They said the Kern River crude gained strength after a major refiner reportedly bought 15,000 bpd of Kern River on a term basis starting in October.
Values for Wilmington were steady at $17.40/17.50.
